data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Thaliah is derived from the Hebrew words 'thal' which means 'dew', and 'yah' which is the short form of the name of God Yahweh. The name Thaliah means 'dew from God'. The name Thaliah carries the meaning “Dew from God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Thaliah usually hope their child will grow to embody dew from god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Thaliah is a reminder that just as dew renews the earth, God renews and refreshes us. It's a name deeply connected to the spirituality of the Hebrew people, and a powerful reminder of God's presence in our lives.

biblical_reference.note: Thaliah is the name of the wife of King Jezebel's son, King Jehoram, in the Old Testament

historical_references.reference: Thaliah, the daughter of King Jotapata, was a prominent figure during the Jewish War led by Simon Bar-Giora against the Roman Empire in the year 66-73 AD. She is known for her courage and her role in the defense of Jerusalem. Thaliah was captured by the Romans and taken to Rome as a slave. She was later released and returned to Jerusalem, where she continued to support the Jewish cause.
historical_references.context: Jewish War against the Roman Empire

historical_references.reference: Thaliah was also a name borne by several saints in the Christian tradition. Saint Thaliah of the Thebaid was a desert mother and a disciple of Saint Macarius the Great. She is said to have lived in the 4th century AD and is venerated in the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches. Saint Thaliah of Rome was a martyr who lived in the late 3rd or early 4th century AD. She is believed to have been a virgin and was martyred during the persecution of Christians under Emperor Diocletian.
